events.title: St. Bernard preaches the Second Crusade at Vézelay
events.shortBlurb: At the pope's bidding, the abbot of Clairvaux roused France to a new crusade, and the king of France took the cross…
body: On 31 March 1146, Palm Sunday, St. Bernard of Clairvaux preached the Second Crusade on a hillside at Vézelay in Burgundy, before King Louis VII of France and a great multitude. Pope Eugene III, once Bernard's own monk, had commissioned him to summon Christendom after the fall of the County of Edessa.

So many pressed forward to take the cross that Bernard, having run out of the cloth crosses prepared, is said to have torn up his own habit to make more. The king and many nobles vowed to go. The crusade that followed ended in failure, a bitter disappointment that weighed heavily on Bernard's last years.
